Commentary.Commentary: Back with the chase! The players of Hong Kong, China, come out and form a final huddle before they spread out to take their respective positions. Also, walk out the two openers of Sri Lanka, where Pathum Nissanka will open the innings alongside Kusal Mendis. Yasim Murtaza has the new ball in his hands, and he will start the proceedings. Here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Sri Lanka bowled 42 dot balls, yet gave away 13 extras, which can prove costly in a game of fine margins. So here we are - 149/4 on the board. Will Sri Lanka’s batters make this a stroll, or can Hong Kong, China, produce the spells of their lives to make this chase a thriller? On this slow pitch, the Powerplay batting will be Sri Lanka’s best bet, using fielding restrictions to kill the game early. Let's see how it goes. The chase is about to begin, so hop up.

That control was broken by the partnership between Anshy Rath and Nizakat Khan. Rath anchored with 48, while Nizakat found timely boundaries, adding a crucial 61 runs for the third wicket. Rath fell just short of his fifty, undone by Chameera, and skipper Yasim Murtaza didn’t last long either, dismissed by Shanaka on his second ball. But Nizakat kept his calm, shifting gears in the final overs to finish unbeaten on 52 off 38 balls to drag his team close to 150.

The innings began with drama in the Powerplay. Zeeshan Ali got a lifeline on the fourth ball when an LBW decision was overturned, and then another when Chameera dropped him, all in the first over. Still, the reprieve didn’t last long as Dushmantha Chameera struck, removing Zeeshan for 23. By the end of six overs, Hong Kong, China, were 42/1, steady but not flying. Babar Hayat struggled to get going, falling to Hasaranga, and the Lankans looked on top at that time, where the ball was holding onto the surface for the spinners.

150 to chase? A TRICKY, TESTING, and perhaps just about COMPETITIVE total on a slow Dubai deck. Could it be enough for Hong Kong, China, to cause an upset? Their innings had bright moments but also lacked acceleration at crucial phases, finishing with 149/4. Meanwhile, Sri Lanka’s bowlers were sharp in patches, but they let the game drift in the middle and at the death, where Nizakat Khan's unbeaten 52 gave his team some hope. Now, it’s all about whether their bowlers can defend this or if Sri Lanka’s openers will crush the chase early in the Powerplay.

No, they can't! However, this is still a fantastic effort from them against a top side. Maheesh Theekshana floats it up, full and on off, Nizakat Khan lofts it down to long off for just one. Commentary.Commentary: We are all set to begin now! The Sri Lankan players are taking up their respective field positions under the bright lights of the Dubai International Stadium. Zeeshan Ali and Anshy Rath are the two openers for Hong Kong, China. Nuwan Thushara, with his slinging action, has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...

Not far away from the first ball now, but before that, the players from the sides make their way out to the middle and line up for the national anthems. It will be Hong Kong, China's first, followed by the national anthem of Sri Lanka.

PITCH REPORT - Roshan Abeysinghe is pitchside. He says that it is a brand new pitch, but a bit dry as well. Russel Arnold joins him and agrees with him.  Adds that there are a few cracks, and we can expect a tennis-ball bounce. Says that the spinners will have a say and chasing is the better option here, but also does not expect it to change much.

Yasim Murtaza, the skipper of Hong Kong, China, says that his team did really well in the last game and they want to repeat the same performance tonight. On team combinations, he confirms one change, with Kalhan Challu making way for Shahid Wasif. Speaking about the approach, he explains that while winning games is important, work ethic remains a priority for the side. On their chances, he admits that they cannot qualify for the Super Four because of a low net run rate, even if they win this match. However, he adds that the team is quite satisfied with their performances in the last two games and now wants to finish the tournament on a high note.

The skipper of Sri Lanka, Charith Asalanka, says that it looks like a decent pitch and they prefer chasing. Adds that he feels the pitch is a bit drier and could be a bit slower. Mentions that the last game was almost perfect, but they will not take any opponent lightly. Informs that Maheesh Theekshana is back in the team in place of Matheesha Pathirana.

Sri Lanka (Playing XI) - Pathum Nissanka, Kusal Mendis (WK), Kamil Mishara, Kusal Perera, Dasun Shanaka, Charith Asalanka (C), Kamindu Mendis, Wanindu Hasaranga, Dushmantha Chameera, Nuwan Thushara, and Maheesh Theekshana (In place of Matheesha Pathirana).

Hong Kong, China (Playing XI) - Zeeshan Ali (WK), Anshy Rath, Babar Hayat, Nizakat Khan, Yasim Murtaza (C), Aizaz Khan, Kinchit Shah, Shahid Wasif (In place of Kalhan Challu), Ehsan Khan, Ayush Shukla, and Ateeq Iqbal.
TOSS - The flip of the coin lands in favour of Sri Lanka, and the skipper, Charith Asalanka, has elected to FIELD first.

Meanwhile, in the first match of today's doubleheader in Abu Dhabi, the United Arab Emirates responded brilliantly against Oman after being sent in to bat first in a crucial match, with their openers Alishan Sharafu and Muhammad Waseem laying a solid foundation. After both sides lost their opening encounters and faced a potential tournament exit, the pressure was and has been immense. The UAE batters, however, didn't buckle, with Sharafu scoring a quickfire 51 and Waseem an impressive 69, helping their team post a challenging total of 172/5. While Oman's bowlers struggled to make early breakthroughs, Jiten Ramanandi was a standout, claiming two key wickets. Now, Oman face a steep chase, needing 173 runs to keep their Super Four hopes alive.

So, what can we expect tonight? Sri Lanka will want to play to win and build momentum ahead of their Afghanistan clash to sort out their place for the Super Four. For Hong Kong, China, it’s their last shot at making a statement before heading home. A slow pitch, spin on offer, and two sides with very different agendas, and it has set up for a fascinating contest. Can Hong Kong, China script an upset, or will Sri Lanka cruise? That’s the question. With that to keep, stick around for the toss and team lineups!

On the flip side, what about Hong Kong, China? What do they need? Win, runs, partnerships, fortunes, and most importantly, belief. Their batting has been patchy, where Nizakat Khan and Zeeshan Ali showed glimpses against Bangladesh, but collapses have hurt them. Their seamers, Ayush Shukla and Ateeq Iqbal, have been bright spots early on, but they struggle to choke runs in the middle. Can Ehsan Khan’s off-spin trouble Sri Lanka’s left-hand heavy middle order? That might just be their only shot at a miracle.

Let’s know a bit about the lions. What does Sri Lanka need? They need consistency, something that has often deserted them in big tournaments. Their bowlers looked fierce with the new ball in the opener, and Wanindu Hasaranga’s return gave them control in the middle overs. Pathum Nissanka and Kamil Mishara are in form at the top, but the middle order still looks fragile. Could they bring in Maheesh Theekshana to exploit a spin-friendly pitch? That’s the big call.

Hello and welcome to Dubai for the only doubleheader of this Asia Cup 2025. It’s Sri Lanka against Hong Kong, China in the second game of the day. Just another clash? Pretty much no, as the stakes are very high where one team wants to clear their objectives for Super Four, while the other side is desperate for a turnaround. How do they stack up? Sri Lanka are coming in high on confidence after crushing Bangladesh, while Hong Kong, China are staring at the exit door with two straight defeats. Head-to-head? This is the first-ever meeting between the two in any format in international cricket.
... MATCH DAY ...

Asia Cup 2025 shifts back to Dubai for a Group B clash between Sri Lanka and Hong Kong, China. This is the final league game for Yasim Murtaza's side, who are staring at elimination after two successive defeats. Even if they manage to upset an in-form Sri Lankan unit, their hopes of progressing will still rest on other results, which is a tall order. For a team with limited exposure at multilateral events, Hong Kong, China have shown signs of growth across their two outings. They were comprehensively beaten by Afghanistan in the opener, but looked far more assured against Bangladesh, even though they eventually fell short. That is often the journey of a developing side, learning step by step against stronger opposition and tougher conditions. Their biggest worry had been the constant fall of wickets, but the previous match offered promise as the batting unit stitched together some useful partnerships, with Zeeshan Ali and Nizakat Khan contributing handy runs. At number three, Babar Hayat remains the pillar of their batting, and much will depend on him to deliver a standout knock if Hong Kong, China are to push Sri Lanka. Bowling-wise, Ayush Shukla has been among the wickets, but has been a touch expensive as well. It’s important for them to put on some control during the death overs as they have leaked runs in that critical phase. Overall, a more improved performance from these blokes will surely boost more confidence in the whole squad. Sri Lanka step in with confidence sky-high after dismantling Bangladesh in their previous outing. It was dominance from the very first ball, with every department clicking in sync. The pace of Dushmantha Chameera and Nuwan Thushara has given them early breakthroughs, while Wanindu Hasaranga's timely return from injury has added bite and variety to their attack. Matheesha Pathirana has been a bit expensive at times, but that comes with the style he bowls, and the team will be hoping for more control from him moving forward. With the bat, the top order has been in fine form, as Pathum Nissanka and Kusal Mendis continue to deliver match-winning knocks. The emergence of Kamil Mishara at number three has been a major boost, providing solidity at a key position and easing the burden on the middle order. With bat and ball both firing, Sri Lanka look like a team growing stronger with each match in this tournament. Interestingly, this is the first-ever time these two sides will meet in the T20I format, or for a fact, in any format of cricket. Hence, both teams are unaware of the challenges they are going to face. It will be interesting to see how the Hong Kong, China batters face the Sri Lankan bowling attack and how their bowlers operate against a full-ledged and in-form Sri Lankan top order. The Sri Lankans have a strong record in Dubai as they have won five out of 8 T20Is, and this is the same venue where they clinched the 2022 Asia Cup by defeating Pakistan. Of course, the Lankans will stride out as clear favorites, and for Hong Kong, China, it is all about stringing together a strong performance to throw some challenge to their counterparts, and more importantly, gain as much knowledge as they can with this kind of exposure to a variety of international sides. An exciting clash is on the cards.
